This week, desk rules for kennel doors
This section covers the main rule first, then the reasons

Companion Animal Travel Desk: kennel access and passenger handling

This section keeps boarding, check-in, and handoff decisions steady so animals stay secure and travelers get a clean answer from Aurelia Skyways. Staff must keep kennel doors closed unless the animal is being placed, removed, or inspected, and every touchpoint should be calm, direct, and documented in plain language. When a traveler is worried, the senior coordinator listens first, then checks the facts before promising any next step. <<FACT F109>> The team should not guess at causes, and it should never pass a pet along when a latch, label, or release step looks uncertain.

If the animal shows stress, the desk slows the process, reduces noise, and asks for a fresh check from the safety coordinator. Staff do not crowd the kennel, tap the crate, or use a sudden motion that may escalate the problem. A traveler may be given a short explanation of the hold while the desk confirms the condition and decides whether the trip can continue as planned. If a delay starts at the desk, the record needs the exact reason, the staff response, and any follow-up note that helps the next shift pick up fast.

The same calm standard applies at transfer and arrival. Cabin or cargo handoff must match the tag, the booking notes, and the visible condition of the carrier, with a second look when anything seems off. Any concern about ventilation, locking hardware, wet bedding, or agitation gets moved to the safety coordinator right away. Supervisors should back the front line by keeping the message short, accurate, and respectful, because the desk loses time when staff improvise or argue.

Use clear language, keep the route open for the next handoff, and stay focused on the animal before the schedule. Report unresolved issues to the duty supervisor or the Companion Animal Travel Desk manager.
